solutions.question: 1(a)
solutions.latex:
Four strips across $12$ m give $h=3$. By the trapezoidal rule:

$$\begin{aligned} A &\approx \dfrac{3}{2}\left(6+2(7+12+8)+10\right) \\ &= 105 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ A

solutions.question: 1(b)
solutions.latex:
Vertical asymptote where $x+4=0$: $x=-4$. As $x\to\pm\infty$, $\dfrac{1}{x+4}\to 0$, so the horizontal asymptote is $y=2$.

$x$-intercept: $2+\dfrac{1}{x+4}=0$, so $x+4=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, giving $(-4.5,\,0)$.

$y$-intercept: $y=2+\dfrac{1}{4}$, giving $(0,\,2.25)$.

\exfigure{1601_q1_s1}
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Correct sketch: correct shape, asymptotes $x=-4$ and $y=2$, and $x$- and $y$-intercepts; 2: Two of correct shape, correct asymptotes, correct intercepts, or equivalent merit; 1: One of correct shape, correct asymptotes, correct intercepts, or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 1(d)
solutions.latex:
Amplitude $2$, period $\dfrac{2\pi}{\frac{1}{2}}=4\pi$, reflected in the $x$-axis: on $0\le x\le 2\pi$ the curve rises from $(0,\,-2)$ through $(\pi,\,0)$ to $(2\pi,\,2)$.

\exfigure{1601_q1_s2}
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correct sketch with correct shape, amplitude and period, including end points; 1: Correct shape and amplitude, or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 2(a)
solutions.latex:
$y=\sin 2\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ is $y=\sin 2x$ shifted $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ left, so it has period $\pi$ and crosses the $x$-axis going up at $x=-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

The next upward crossing is at $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}+\pi=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, which rules out A and D; B is decreasing at $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

$\therefore$ C

solutions.question: 2(b)
solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} y &= x^3-3x^2-9x+4 \\ y' &= 3x^2-6x-9 \\ &= 3(x^2-2x-3) \\ &= 3(x-3)(x+1) \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} y'' &= 6x-6 \\ &= 6(x-1) \end{aligned}$$

For stationary points $y'=0$: $x=3$ or $x=-1$, giving $y=-23$ or $y=9$.

At $(-1,\,9)$: $y''=6(-1-1)=-12<0$

$\therefore$ local maximum at $(-1,\,9)$.

At $(3,\,-23)$: $y''=6(3-1)=12>0$

$\therefore$ local minimum at $(3,\,-23)$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Correct answer; 2: Finds both stationary points, or equivalent merit; 1: Finds $y'$ and $y''$, or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 2(b)
solutions.latex:
For inflections $y''=0$:

$$\begin{aligned} 6(x-1) &= 0 \\ x &= 1 \end{aligned}$$

so the possible point is $(1,\,-7)$.

Test:

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} x & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \hline y'' & -6 & 0 & 6 \end{array}$$

Change in concavity.

$\therefore$ point of inflection at $(1,\,-7)$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correct answer, showing the change in concavity; 1: Finds $x=1$, $(1,\,-7)$, or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 2(b)
solutions.latex:
Cubic with $y$-intercept $(0,\,4)$, local maximum $(-1,\,9)$, point of inflection $(1,\,-7)$ and local minimum $(3,\,-23)$.

\exfigure{1601_q2_s1}
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correct sketch showing the stationary points and the point of inflection; 1: Correct shape and $y$-intercept, or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 3(a)
solutions.latex:
The region on $-3\le x\le 0$ is below the $x$-axis, so its area is $-\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{0} f(x)\,dx=\int_{0}^{-3} f(x)\,dx$.

The other two regions are above the axis.

$$\text{Area}=\int_{-7}^{-3} f(x)\,dx+\int_{0}^{-3} f(x)\,dx+\int_{0}^{3} f(x)\,dx$$

$\therefore$ D

solutions.question: 3(b)
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correct answer; 1: Correct primitive (either form), or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 3(c)
solutions.latex:
Circle: circumference $=x$.

$$\begin{aligned} 2\pi r &= x \\ r &= \dfrac{x}{2\pi} \end{aligned}$$

Area of circle $=\pi\left(\dfrac{x}{2\pi}\right)^2$

Square: perimeter $=100-x$, so one side $=\dfrac{100-x}{4}$.

Area of square $=\left(\dfrac{100-x}{4}\right)^2$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total area} &= \dfrac{\pi x^2}{4\pi^2}+\left(\dfrac{100-x}{4}\right)^2 \\ &= \dfrac{x^2}{4\pi}+\dfrac{(100-x)^2}{16} \end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correct derivation; 1: Finds the area of the circle or the area of the square, or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 3(c)
solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{x^2}{4\pi}+\dfrac{(100-x)^2}{16} \\ A' &= \dfrac{2x}{4\pi}-\dfrac{2(100-x)}{16} \\ &= \dfrac{x}{2\pi}-\dfrac{100-x}{8} \end{aligned}$$

For stationary points $A'=0$:

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{x}{2\pi}-\dfrac{100-x}{8} &= 0 \\ \dfrac{4x-\pi(100-x)}{8\pi} &= 0 \\ 4x-100\pi+\pi x &= 0 \\ x(4+\pi) &= 100\pi \\ x &= \dfrac{100\pi}{4+\pi} \\ &= 43.99\ldots \\ &\approx 44 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$

Check $44$ cm is a minimum turning point:

$$\begin{aligned} A'' &= \dfrac{1}{2\pi}+\dfrac{1}{8} \\ &= 0.28 \\ &> 0 \text{ for all } x \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ $44$ cm is a minimum.

$\therefore$ the wire should be cut at $44$ cm to minimise the total area of the square and the circle.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Correct answer, with the minimum verified; 2: Finds $x\approx 44$ cm, or equivalent merit; 1: Finds $A'$, or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 4(a)
solutions.latex:
Divide numerator and denominator by $x^2$:

$$f(x)=\dfrac{1+\frac{1}{x^2}}{\frac{4}{x^2}-1}$$

As $x\to\pm\infty$, $f(x)\to\dfrac{1}{-1}=-1$, so the horizontal asymptote is $y=-1$.

$\therefore$ B

solutions.question: 4(b)
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Correct answer; 1: Correctly factorises the quadratic, or equivalent merit

solutions.question: 4(d)
solutions.latex:
Let $B$ be the area of the blue region, $W$ the area of the small rectangle and $A$ the area of the big rectangle.

$$\begin{aligned} B &= \int_a^b x^n\,dx \\ &= \dfrac{1}{n+1}\left[x^{n+1}\right]_a^b \\ &= \dfrac{1}{n+1}\left(b^{n+1}-a^{n+1}\right) \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} W &= a\times a^n \\ &= a^{n+1} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} A &= b\times b^n \\ &= b^{n+1} \end{aligned}$$

The big rectangle is made up of the blue region, the red region ($3B$) and the small rectangle:

$$\begin{aligned} A &= B+3B+W \\ &= 4B+W \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} b^{n+1} &= \dfrac{4}{n+1}\left(b^{n+1}-a^{n+1}\right)+a^{n+1} \\ b^{n+1}-a^{n+1} &= \dfrac{4}{n+1}\left(b^{n+1}-a^{n+1}\right) \\ 1 &= \dfrac{4}{n+1} \\ 4 &= n+1 \\ n &= 3 \end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: Correct answer; 3: Sets up the correct relationship between the areas, or equivalent merit; 2: Finds the blue area and both rectangle areas, or equivalent merit; 1: Finds the blue area or both rectangle areas, or equivalent merit
